item.title: Usino/Bundi district gets new finance manager
item.description: The Usino/ Bundi District Development Authority has welcomed a new era in its financial administration, following the formal handover/ takeover of the District Finance Manager's position. The change brings to the end two decades of service by outgoing DFM Samuel Abel.
item.content:encoded:
The Usino/ Bundi District Development Authority has welcomed a new era in its financial administration, following the formal handover/ takeover of the District Finance Manager's position.

The change brings to the end two decades of service by outgoing DFM Samuel Abel.

The official ceremony, held at the District Office in Walium, saw Mr Abel formally hand over the responsibilities to his successor, Helen Kavo, who brings more than 30 years of professional experience in the finance sector.

The transition was witnessed by Deputy Secretary of the Department of Finance's Sub-national Division, Gabi Kila, who travelled from Port Moresby, District Administrator and Chief Executive Officer Johnson Wai, district management, finance and administration officers, Local Level Government representatives and other invited stakeholders.

The ceremony recognised Mr Abel's longstanding contribution to the district's financial administration while formally welcoming Ms Kavo to take on the important responsibility of overseeing the district's financial operations.

Addressing the gathering, Mr Kila highlighted the importance of teamwork and institutional continuity in public administration and acknowledged Mr Abel for his commitment, dedication, and years of service to the people of Usino, Bundi, and Gama in the area of public finance.

Mr Kila also extended his best wishes to Ms Kavo, as she assumes the responsibilities of the district's new Finance Manager.

In his farewell remarks, Mr Abel expressed sincere appreciation to the Member for Usino Bundi, Vincent Kumura, the District Administration, colleagues, stakeholders and the people of the district for their support and cooperation throughout his more than 20 years of service.

He acknowledged that his time in the district finance office had been strengthened by teamwork, professional relationships, and the collective commitment of officers and stakeholders towards advancing the district's development aspirations.

Welcoming his successor, he wished Ms Kavo well as she takes responsibility for leading the Finance Division, expressing confidence in her ability to continue the work of strengthening the district's financial administration.

Incoming District Finance Manager, Ms Kavo expressed gratitude to the Department of Finance, PNG Treasury, the District Administration, and all stakeholders who contributed to a smooth transition.

Transferred from Port Moresby, Ms Kavo brings more than 30 years of professional experience in the finance sector to her new role.

She specifically acknowledged Mr. Abel for his cooperation and support during the transition, recognising the importance of a proper handover in ensuring continuity in the district's financial administration.

Her appointment comes at an important time when effective financial management, accountabilit, and coordination are critical to supporting government-funded programmes and development activities throughout the district.

Delivering the keynote address, District Administrator and CEO Johnson Wai emphasised that the handover/ takeover was more than a routine administrative exercise, describing it as an essential accountability process to safeguard public resources and maintain institutional continuity.

Mr Wai acknowledged Mr Abel's more than 20 years of service, particularly his contribution to managing government grants, maintaining financial records, supporting financial reporting and acquittals, and providing financial guidance to the district and its three Local Level Governments.

He challenged the incoming Finance Manager to uphold the highest standards of professionalism, integrity, financial discipline, and compliance with the Public Finance Management framework.

Mr Wai stressed that the Finance Division must be an enabler of development and service delivery rather than an administrative obstacle to progress.

"Finance is not there to block development. Finance is there to enable development within the rules. We must ensure that public funds are properly managed while allowing essential services and development projects to reach our people," Mr Wai said.

He further encouraged Ms Kavo to strengthen the capacity of district and LLG finance personnel through mentoring, teamwork, and improved financial management systems.

The CEO assured her of the full support and cooperation of the District Administration and management team as she takes up her new responsibilities.

As part of the official transition, both officers undertook the formal transfer and verification of essential financial and administrative records.

These included bank statements, cashbooks, outstanding financial commitments, acquittals, asset registers, audit reports, payment records, office keys, and relevant financial system access.

Meanwhile, the office of the local MP also acknowledged Mr Abel's valuable contributions and more than 20 years of dedicated service to the district.

The leadership transition highlights the importance of continuity in public administration, where individual responsibilities may change, but the obligation to manage public resources responsibly and serve communities remains constant.

As Usino Bundi Gama advances its development agenda, the District Administration and Finance Division will be expected to maintain close collaboration to ensure that public funds are managed in accordance with established financial regulations and that development priorities receive the necessary financial support.

item.title: Simbai youths lead community surrender program
item.description: Youths in the Simbai LLG area of the Middle Ramu district have taken a positive step towards restoring peace and good order by voluntarily surrendering their home-brewing bottles on Monday. They also participated in the uprooting of marijuana plants during the community surrender program at Simbai station.
item.content:encoded:
Youths in the Simbai LLG area of the Middle Ramu district have taken a positive step towards restoring peace and good order by voluntarily surrendering their home-brewing bottles on Monday.

They also participated in the uprooting of marijuana plants during the community surrender program at Simbai station.

The event was witnessed by police personnel from Madang Town, whose attendance at Simbai was facilitated through the support of Middle Ramu District Development Authority (MRDDA) under the chairmanship of local MP, Kansol Harwai Kamdaru.

The program also received support from Simbai LLG president, Nehemiah Kapa, and other local community leaders, who contributed to the community engagement and reconciliation efforts.

The initiative follows ongoing social problems, community tensions, and law and order challenges, including the burning of the temporary council chamber.

It also builds on a previous successful reconciliation between Simbai Central and Kaigen Zones, marking an important step towards rebuilding trust, forgiveness, and unity amongst the communities.

The program aims to encourage youths to take responsibility, discourage illegal activities, and strengthen cooperation between communities, police and government authorities across all four zones of Simbai LLG, including Simbai, Kaigen, Asai and Kairong.

The initiative represents a collective commitment to restoring peace, protecting public infrastructure, rebuilding community relationships, and creating a safer environment for government workers, service providers, and development partners.

The ultimate goal, however; is to restore Simbai's dignity, strengthen public confidence, and ensure that education and other government services, plus development opportunities, reach the people without fear or disruption.

This program marks a positive step towards a new beginning for Simbai, where peace, unity, respect for the law, and community responsibility become the foundation for lasting development.

Leaders in the area said homebrew, marijuana, sorcery, and unsettled land matters are major issues contributing to the detriment in law and order in Middle Ramu district.

item.title: Cancer care is significant milestone
item.description: Port Moresby General Hospital (PMGH) in collaboration with the Flowtint Group successfully completed the commissioning of its Computed Tomography (CT) Simulator, with international technical support over the past five days. The commissioning involved collaboration between international and local Medical Physicists, bringing together expertise from Australia, Sri Lanka and Papua New Guinea. As part
item.content:encoded:
Port Moresby General Hospital (PMGH) in collaboration with the Flowtint Group successfully completed the commissioning of its Computed Tomography (CT) Simulator, with international technical support over the past five days. The commissioning involved collaboration between international and local Medical Physicists, bringing together expertise from Australia, Sri Lanka and Papua New Guinea.

As part of the commissioning process, the Medical Physicists established baseline machine performance, conducted quality assurance measurements and verified that the CT Simulator met the required tolerance levels for optimal image quality. Importantly, the team characterized the relationship between CT Hounsfield Units (HU) and Relative Electron Density (RED) across different tissue-equivalent materials. These values were later incorporated into the Treatment Planning System (TPS) to facilitate accurate radiation dose calculations for radiotherapy treatment planning.

In a statement, P-M-G-H Chief Executive Officer Dr. Paki Molumi said the commissioning results will undergo final technical verification before submission to PMGH Clinical Governance for approval and subsequent release for clinical use.

This achievement represents another significant milestone in strengthening PMGH's capacity to deliver safe, accurate and quality-assured cancer treatment services in Papua New Guinea.

item.title: WHP urged to crown queen before national pageant
item.description: With Mt Hagen set to host the Miss Bird of Paradise Papua New Guinea national pageant in December, organisers are calling for the Western Highlands provincial pageant to be staged first. Chairlady of Miss Bird of Paradise Western Highlands, Delilah Goni, is welcoming the Western Highlands Provincial Government’s support for hosting the national Miss Bird of Paradise Papua New Guinea pageant in Mt
item.content:encoded:
With Mt Hagen set to host the Miss Bird of Paradise Papua New Guinea national pageant in December, organisers are calling for the Western Highlands provincial pageant to be staged first.

Chairlady of Miss Bird of Paradise Western Highlands, Delilah Goni, is welcoming the Western Highlands Provincial Government’s support for hosting the national Miss Bird of Paradise Papua New Guinea pageant in Mt Hagen.

However, Ms Goni says the provincial pageant must come first, with Western Highlands crowning its own queen before moving to the national competition.

The provincial pageant, according to the Miss Westeen Highlands Committee in a statement, was delivered within two weeks (in 2025) under Goni’s leadership and has helped create the opportunity for Western Highlands to host the national event this year.

The committee also stated that crowning a provincial queen is important because it completes the provincial stage before the province moves to the national platform.

With the national pageant scheduled for December in Mt Hagen, the team says time is now critical.

They are making a call for a regular and clear communication between the Western Highlands Provincial Government as the major sponsor and host, the Miss Bird of Paradise management and Chairlady Delilah Goni.

They outlined that the stakeholders need to sit down and agree on the remaining arrangements, including outstanding allowances, the proposed pageant budget and other issues that need to be resolved before the national event.

They stressed that the Provincial Government’s support is appreciated, particularly as preparations are already underway at Sir Mara Haus, where a stage is being prepared to host the national pageant.

The Miss Western Highlands committee says hosting the national Miss Bird of Paradise pageant is a major opportunity for Western Highlands to showcase its culture, tourism and people to the country.

Goni who is the provincial pageant Western Highlands chairlady said the provincial queen must be crowned, outstanding matters settled and the budget agreed on, while preparations for the national pageant continue.

With December fast approaching, the Miss Western Highlands committee say there is no time to lose if Western Highlands is to successfully host the Miss Bird of Paradise Papua New Guinea national pageant.

item.title: Second relief supply dispatch to reach Lovongai and Tikana
item.description: The New Ireland Provincial Government has stepped up its relief distribution programme, with a second batch of supplies now being delivered to communities in Lovongai and Tikana Local Level Governments. The latest dispatch covers communities in Lovongai LLG and Wards 1, 2, 17 and 18 of Tikana, as the provincial government continues its phase-one efforts to assist people affected by difficult condi
item.content:encoded:
The New Ireland Provincial Government has stepped up its relief distribution programme, with a second batch of supplies now being delivered to communities in Lovongai and Tikana Local Level Governments.

The latest dispatch covers communities in Lovongai LLG and Wards 1, 2, 17 and 18 of Tikana, as the provincial government continues its phase-one efforts to assist people affected by difficult conditions, particularly in island communities.

Governor Byron Chan said the ongoing distribution reflected his government's commitment to ensuring that assistance reached people who needed it, regardless of where they lived.

“Our responsibility is to make sure that no community is forgotten. Whether our people live on the islands or on the mainland, they deserve to feel the presence of their government, especially during difficult times,” Governor Chan said.

He said the relief programme was part of a wider effort to ensure government assistance was delivered where it was needed most, with communities and local leaders involved in the process.

Provincial Administrator Dennis Kosam said the Provincial Administration was coordinating the distribution with LLG authorities, ward councillors, community leaders and government officers to ensure supplies reached the intended beneficiaries.

“The delivery of this second batch of relief supplies is another important step in getting assistance to our people. We are working closely with local leaders and communities to ensure the distribution is carried out in an orderly, transparent and accountable manner,” Kosam said.

Kosam said the relief programme would not be limited to the island communities, with mainland areas of the province scheduled to be covered in the next phase.

He said the phased approach was necessary to coordinate transportation, logistics and distribution arrangements across New Ireland's geographically spread communities.

“Our people are at the centre of government. Whether they live on the islands or the mainland, every community matters, and every New Irelander deserves the attention and support of their government,” Kosam said.

The Provincial Administration will continue working with district administrations, LLG authorities, ward councillors and community leaders to prepare for the next batch of the programme.fsctored under the initial K2.5 million in disaster aid from the National Government.

K6 million from the Provincial Services Improvement Program (PSIP) funds have been facortored in the second phase of relief efforts.

Governor Chan and Kosam acknowledged the cooperation of local leaders and communities in facilitating the relief exercise, saying their support was important in ensuring assistance reached the right people.

The Provincial Government said it remained committed to extending relief assistance and essential government services to communities throughout New Ireland Province.

item.title: Revival Centre of PNG celebrates 40 years of ministry in East Sepik
item.description: The Revival Centre of Papua New Guinea (RCPNG) has marked 40 years of Christian ministry in East Sepik Province, commemorating four decades since the church was founded on November 1, 1986. The four-day anniversary celebration commenced on Thursday, October 29, and concluded on Sunday, November 1, 2026, bringing together thousands of church members, pastors, leaders and invited guests to commemora
item.content:encoded:
The Revival Centre of Papua New Guinea (RCPNG) has marked 40 years of Christian ministry in East Sepik Province, commemorating four decades since the church was founded on November 1, 1986.

The four-day anniversary celebration commenced on Thursday, October 29, and concluded on Sunday, November 1, 2026, bringing together thousands of church members, pastors, leaders and invited guests to commemorate the historic milestone.

According to the RCPNG 40th Anniversary Programme Organising Committee, a total of 10,891 church members attended the celebration, including more than 200 pastors and church leaders.

The anniversary also recorded 374 new members who were baptised and officially joined the Revival Centre of Papua New Guinea, marking another milestone in the church's continued growth.

Meanwhile, Momase Regional Pastor Collen Solmen acknowledged the pioneers of the RCPNG Wewak Assembly and all those who contributed to making the four-day anniversary celebration a success.

The church's Founder and Principal Pastor, Godfrey Wippon, encouraged members and leaders to remain committed to their Christian calling and continue spreading the Gospel.

He said, "Keep the Gospel moving, keep going, continue on with the work the Lord has placed in your heart and in your mind."

Pastor Wippon officially closed the 40th anniversary programme with the cutting of the anniversary cake, symbolising four decades of the Revival Centre's establishment and ministry in East Sepik Province.

Since its establishment in 1986, the church has continued its ministry and strengthening the faith of its members and spreading the Gospel among communities across the province.

item.title: Moem clan groups protest over Boram airport land compensation
item.description: Two registered Indigenous Land Groups (ILGs) from Moem village in Ward 9 of Wewak Rural LLG have raised concerns over the Boram airport land compensation process, calling on the East Sepik Provincial Administration to establish the rightful landowners before any compensation payments are made. The Mombui Clan Group and Pose Tamare Clan Group raised their grievances with the East Sepik Provincial A
item.content:encoded:
Two registered Indigenous Land Groups (ILGs) from Moem village in Ward 9 of Wewak Rural LLG have raised concerns over the Boram airport land compensation process, calling on the East Sepik Provincial Administration to establish the rightful landowners before any compensation payments are made.

The Mombui Clan Group and Pose Tamare Clan Group raised their grievances with the East Sepik Provincial Administration this morning, November 6, over land ownership, the identification of customary landowners and the compensation process.

The two groups are demanding a proper Land Investigation Report (LIR) to establish the traditional land boundaries and identify the legitimate landowners of the Boram airport area.

They also want the Provincial Administration to recognise the respective Indigenous Land Groups through proper landowner identification, including the verification of genealogy records and common land boundaries.

Moem Ward 9-member, John Kalsup, told NBC News that the Provincial Administration must first carry out a land investigation report to establish the land boundaries and identify the rightful owners.

“We believe what the East Sepik Provincial Administration must do is a Land Investigation Report (LIR) so we can identify the land boundaries,” Kalsup said.

He further stressed that land compensation payments must be made to the recognised Indigenous Land Groups and not into private company accounts.

The two clan groups have also engaged a lawyer to represent them in the matter and are calling for a proper land mediation process to establish the legitimate customary landowners of Boram airport.

They have also warned that work on the newly constructed road from the CIS area down to Pukpuk bridge will be stopped until the Provincial Administration addresses the outstanding Boram airport land compensation issue, including compensation relating to the airport extension.

Meanwhile, the leaders of the two registered Indigenous Land Groups told NBC News that their lawyer would deliver a Section 5 Notice to the East Sepik Provincial Administration before close of business today.

The notice, under the Claims by and Against the State Act 1996, formally informs the State of their intention to pursue legal action over the Boram airport land compensation dispute.

NBC News is seeking response from the East Sepik Provincial Administration

This is a developing story, and NBC News will continue to follow the matter and provide further updates as more information becomes available.

item.title: Mendi-Munihu district distributes rice to communities
item.description: The Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) has distributed rice bags to families hard-hit by the ongoing El Niño drought that has left many households facing severe food shortages. Mendi-Munihu District Administrator Philip Koka confirmed the distribution, stating that the district used K2.5 million in relief funding provided by the National Government.
item.content:encoded:
The Mendi-Munihu District Development Authority (MMDDA) has distributed rice bags to families hard-hit by the ongoing El Niño drought that has left many households facing severe food shortages.

Mendi-Munihu District Administrator Philip Koka confirmed the distribution, stating that the district used K2.5 million in relief funding provided by the National Government.

Seven Hino trucks loaded with food supplies arrived at the Mendi-Munihu District Office at Six Mile, Tente, with supplies officially distributed to communities in the Upper Mendi Local Level Government (LLG) — making them the first communities in the district to receive the much-needed assistance. After Upper Mendi, Karinz LLG distributed its share and today Lai Valley LLG is distributing its share.

Lai Valley LLG President Manuel Olpa acknowledged the Mendi-Munihu DDA under the leadership of MP Raphael Tonpi for looking into the poor people's need and distributing rice to address the El Niño-induced food shortage.

"But for the ordinary people, the reality is very different. Some will say a bag of rice is not enough — and that may be true. But there are very poor families, families whose gardens and crops have completely failed due to the El Niño drought, who deeply appreciate this effort.

“For them, this rice is not just food, it is hope. It is the difference between going to bed hungry and feeding their children for another day," President Olpa said.

District CEO Mr Koka said while other basic food items were not included in this first round of rice bags, responding to the people's plea for help was critical as many families had gone hungry.

"Addressing the people's plea for help is important. In the second round, the Mendi-Munihu DDA can look at other food items as well. For now, this is from the immediate assistance funding given by the National Government which the MMDDA used to purchase them" Koka said.

The distribution was led by Upper Mendi LLG President Kevin Sapul, together with Karinz LLG President Simon Tolpe and Lai Valley President Manuel Olpa.
